Steadfastness that stops waiting and begins arranging becomes Machination: the same immovable purpose pursued through other people's ignorance, which is why the fall keeps the patience and loses the honesty. Reform that stops persuading and begins purging becomes Zealotry: the principle still correct, the method now the thing being enjoyed. Each fall is exactly what its own virtue does when it will no longer accept a cost — the pragmatist unwilling to wait, the idealist unwilling to be resisted.

[[Correspondences]] Cold end (−1,+1,0): Steadfastness falling to Machination — Ruth and Rosa Parks against Iago and Cardinal Richelieu. Warm end (+1,−1,0): Reform falling to Zealotry — Nehemiah and Abraham Lincoln against Saul of Tarsus and Oliver Cromwell. On the Rose the seats face each other at 15h in orange and 03h in cyan; on the Almanac wheel the axis takes November at 22h — the month of a foiled machination, remembered every fifth day of it.

[[Quote]] "For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost?" (Luke 14:28); "and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?" (Micah 6:8).

Steadfastness.base:
[[Thesis]] Steadfastness is the cold cell of the Pragmatism ↔ Idealism axis: a position kept by not moving, for as long as the keeping takes.

[[Argument]] The seat joins Composure to Loyalty — restraint in the service of a bond — and its acts are almost always small, which is why it is so often mistaken for passivity. Ruth is released from every obligation she has and stays anyway, which is the purest form the seat takes: the bond survives the disappearance of the reason to keep it. Rosa Parks does not move on 1 December 1955, and the whole content of the act is the refusal of a motion, performed once, at a cost that could be calculated in advance. Brienne of Tarth keeps an oath after the woman who took it is dead, which is the modern reading of the same shape — the counterparty gone, the obligation intact. The fall keeps the patience and abandons the honesty. Machination is the same immovable purpose pursued through other people's ignorance: a handkerchief worked for months, a dismissal turned into the ruin of one's rivals in a single November day, a murder and a letter that start a war for a man who says out loud that chaos is a ladder. The discriminator is exact and worth stating: Steadfastness waits in the open and pays for the waiting; Machination waits in the dark and arranges for somebody else to pay.

[[Correspondences]] The cell (−1,+1,0), Composure plus Loyalty, on the Pragmatism ↔ Idealism axis, facing Reform and its fall Zealotry through the centre. On the Rose it takes 15h in orange; on the Almanac wheel its axis holds November at 22h. Archetypal: Ruth against Iago. Historical: Rosa Parks against Cardinal Richelieu. Modern: Brienne of Tarth against Petyr Baelish. Ruth is the recorded Loyalty alternate, seated here where she is exact.

[[Quote]] "Whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge" (Ruth 1:16); "be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord" (1 Corinthians 15:58).

Reform.base:
[[Thesis]] Reform is the warm cell of the Pragmatism ↔ Idealism axis: the world moved because a principle says it must be, by someone willing to pay the bill for moving it.

[[Argument]] The seat joins Vigor to Integrity, and the pairing is what separates it from mere indignation: a rule alone changes nothing, and force alone changes the wrong things. Nehemiah finishes a wall in fifty-two days and, in the same chapters, cancels the debts owed to his own creditor class — the reformer taking the cost onto the party he belongs to, which is the seat's cleanest archetypal act. Lincoln signs the Emancipation Proclamation on the first day of 1863, an instrument whose whole force is that a principle was written down and made law. The modern reading is deliberately unglamorous: a schoolgirl founds an abolitionist society against everyone's amusement, and the amusement is part of the argument. The fall arrives when the correction stops persuading and starts purging. Zealotry is Reform that will no longer accept resistance: the archetypal reading names itself, since the persecutor of the church described his own zeal in a letter before the road to Damascus changed it; the historical reading reforms by purge, from Drogheda in 1649 to government by Major-Generals; the modern one refuses the bargain and dies for the refusal, never compromising even in the face of the end of the world. The line between the two readings is not the goal but the method, and the fall always believes it is still the virtue.

[[Correspondences]] The cell (+1,−1,0), Vigor plus Integrity, on the Pragmatism ↔ Idealism axis, facing Steadfastness and its fall Machination through the centre. On the Rose it takes 03h in cyan; on the Almanac wheel its axis holds November at 22h. Archetypal: Nehemiah against Saul of Tarsus. Historical: Abraham Lincoln against Oliver Cromwell. Modern: Hermione Granger against Rorschach. The vertex directly above this cell adds Humility and produces the Principled Reformer; add Dignity instead and the same drive becomes the Visionary Founder.

[[Quote]] "Let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream" (Amos 5:24); against "concerning zeal, persecuting the church; touching the righteousness which is in the law, blameless" (Philippians 3:6).

Person ↔ Cause.base:
[[Thesis]] The third edge axis asks what a life is spent ON — a person who can be named, or a principle that outlives every person serving it.

[[Argument]] Here Activation is silent and the two committed axes are Moral Scope and Self-Regard. The cold end joins Loyalty to Humility: a bond served by someone who does not need to be seen serving it, which is Devotion. The warm end joins Integrity to Dignity: a principle held by someone who knows his own standing well enough to answer for it, which is Conviction. The pairing explains a difficulty this canon meets everywhere — that a life spent on a person and a life spent on a cause look identical from outside, and diverge only when the two conflict. The falls name what each end does when the conflict arrives. Devotion becomes Martyrdom when the giving stops being for the person and starts being for the giving, the point at which what was protected has become secondary to the act of paying. Conviction becomes Dogmatism when the principle stops answering questions and starts refusing them, so that the rule survives its own reason. Both falls keep the whole strength of their virtue, which is why they are dangerous and why neither is drawn as weakness.

[[Correspondences]] Cold end (0,+1,−1): Devotion falling to Martyrdom — Moses, Janusz Korczak and Alfred Pennyworth against Samson, Marcus Antonius and Severus Snape. Warm end (0,−1,+1): Conviction falling to Dogmatism — Elijah, Martin Luther and Steve Rogers against Creon, Joseph Stalin and Dolores Umbridge. Both cells also ride the Character wheel, which is the Cube read at depth zero — Devotion on its green arm, Conviction on its rose one. On the Rose they face each other at 11h in yellow and 23h in purple; on the Almanac wheel the axis takes July at 14h, the month of the Bastille and the Fourth.

[[Quote]] "Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends" (John 15:13); against "He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me" (Matthew 10:37).

Hearth ↔ Desert.base:
[[Thesis]] The fourth edge axis asks what a person does with weight he actually has: spends it on a household, or lays it down and walks out.

[[Argument]] Activation is again at measure, and the committed axes are Moral Scope and Self-Regard in the opposite pairing to Person ↔ Cause. The cold end joins Loyalty to Dignity: a bond honoured from a position of strength, which is Patronage — standing converted into somebody else's standing. The warm end joins Integrity to Humility: a principle kept by subtraction, which is Renunciation — the crown, the cloak and the purse put down rather than broken. The two ends are the only honest answers to the same question, and the axis refuses to rank them: a house that shelters is not a failure of asceticism, and a man who owns nothing is not a failure of generosity. Their falls are again their own excesses. Patronage becomes Favoritism when the weight is spent on the bond instead of the work, the exact point at which raising your own turns into preferring your own. Renunciation becomes Mortification when the subtraction outlives its purpose and begins to consume the man performing it, so that the emptying has become the point. The Hearth's fall keeps too much; the Desert's fall gives past the end of giving.

[[Correspondences]] Cold end (0,+1,+1): Patronage falling to Favoritism — Boaz, Lorenzo de' Medici and Charles Xavier against King Lear, Nicolae Ceaușescu and Denethor II. Warm end (0,−1,−1): Renunciation falling to Mortification — John the Baptist, Thomas More and Obi-Wan Kenobi against Father Ferapont, Simone Weil and Silas. Both cells ride the Character wheel as its orange and cyan arms. On the Rose they face each other at 13h in yellow and 01h in purple; on the Almanac wheel the axis takes January at 2h, deep winter, when a hearth is the whole argument.

[[Quote]] "But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith" (1 Timothy 5:8); against "The foxes have holes, and the birds of the air have nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head" (Matthew 8:20).

Lion ↔ Lamb.base:
[[Thesis]] The fifth edge axis asks how high a person aims, and it seats the two answers on the line where Activation and Self-Regard are committed and judgment says nothing.

[[Argument]] The cold end joins Composure to Humility: strength held still by someone who does not press his own claim, which is Meekness — a word this canon uses in its old sense of power under government rather than in its modern sense of timidity. The warm end joins Vigor to Dignity: force spent by someone who knows his own worth, which is Aspiration — the ceiling raised on purpose. Because Moral Scope is at measure, neither end is a claim about what a person judges by; both are claims about altitude. The falls part company sharply. Meekness that continues past the point where a man should still have wanted something becomes Despair, the fall in which the lowering has reached the person himself. Aspiration that continues past its own measure becomes Megalomania, the ceiling raised over other people rather than over the work. One disarming sentence is owed wherever this axis is taught, because the names carry an old freight: Scripture gives BOTH titles to Christ, the Lion of the tribe of Judah who is also the Lamb — so the axis names a human split of what the centre unites, and the Lion end's seat on the warm side moralizes nothing. No colour on this cube is good and no colour is evil.

[[Correspondences]] Cold end (−1,0,−1): Meekness falling to Despair — Isaac and Francis of Assisi against Cain and Vincent van Gogh. Warm end (+1,0,+1): Aspiration falling to Megalomania — Daedalus and Muhammad Ali against Icarus and Alexander the Great. On the Rose the two seats face each other at 09h in green and 21h in rose; on the Almanac wheel the axis takes March at 6h — the spring equinox, from which the computus defines the Lamb's own feast.

[[Quote]] "Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the Root of David, hath prevailed... and lo, in the midst of the throne, a Lamb as it had been slain" (Revelation 5:5–6); "Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth" (Matthew 5:5).

Meekness.base:
[[Thesis]] Meekness is the cold cell of the Lion ↔ Lamb axis: strength kept under government by someone who does not press his own claim — power restrained, never power absent.

[[Argument]] The seat joins Composure to Humility, and the canon uses the word in its old sense on purpose, because the modern sense would make the cell a synonym for weakness and there is no seat on this cube for that. Isaac carries the wood up Moriah and does not resist, which is the archetypal act: the strength to refuse is present and is not used. Francis of Assisi resigns the leadership of the order he founded in 1220 and calls himself the least of the brothers — an act of subtraction performed by the one man whose claim was unanswerable. Frodo carries what the great may not touch, which is the modern reading of the same asymmetry: the least equipped bearer is the only possible one. The fall is the one place on this cube where the Colour Law has to be read out loud. Despair is Meekness continued until the lowering reaches the person himself, and Scripture's first instance of it is a sentence rather than an act — a punishment declared greater than the man can bear. The historical reading is seated on the letters of July 1890, and it is a station, never a verdict: an illness is a tragedy and a fall is a position on a line, and neither is a judgment on a life. Théoden proves the doctrine from the other side — a king in whom the acting had stopped is raised out of the seat, which is what a station means.

[[Correspondences]] The cell (−1,0,−1), Composure plus Humility, on the Lion ↔ Lamb axis, facing Aspiration and its fall Megalomania through the centre. On the Rose it takes 09h in green; on the Almanac wheel its axis holds March at 6h, the equinox from which the Lamb's feast is computed. Archetypal: Isaac against Cain. Historical: Francis of Assisi against Vincent van Gogh. Modern: Frodo Baggins against Théoden. Moral Scope is at measure here: the seat says nothing about what a person judges by.

[[Quote]] "and after the fire a still small voice" (1 Kings 19:12); against "My punishment is greater than I can bear" (Genesis 4:13).

Aspiration.base:
[[Thesis]] Aspiration is the warm cell of the Lion ↔ Lamb axis: a ceiling raised on purpose by someone who knows his own worth and spends it on the climb.

[[Argument]] The seat joins Vigor to Dignity, and its archetypal holder is the maker rather than the flyer: wings built against a king's ceiling, and with them an instruction to keep the MIDDLE course — this canon's own law of measure, spoken by the man who invented the means of breaking it. That is why the cell and its fall are the same pair of wings. Muhammad Ali says he is the greatest before it is true, which is the seat's exact grammar: a claim made in advance and then paid for. Rocky Balboa asks only to go the distance, which is the same aspiration with the boast removed and the standard kept. The fall is the climb continued past the work and over other people. Icarus takes his father's wings higher; Alexander accepts proskynesis and the sonship of Zeus-Ammon after Siwa in 331 BC, which is the historical moment a man stops raising his own ceiling and starts raising himself above everyone else's; the modern reading builds a defence for the whole world in secret and produces the thing the world then has to survive. Megalomania keeps every gram of the virtue's energy — that is precisely its danger, and the reason the seat is drawn as one direction rather than as two.

[[Correspondences]] The cell (+1,0,+1), Vigor plus Dignity, on the Lion ↔ Lamb axis, facing Meekness and its fall Despair through the centre. On the Rose it takes 21h in rose; on the Almanac wheel its axis holds March at 6h. Archetypal: Daedalus against Icarus. Historical: Muhammad Ali against Alexander the Great. Modern: Rocky Balboa against Tony Stark. Add Loyalty to this cell and it becomes the Charismatic Champion; add Integrity and it becomes the Visionary Founder.

[[Quote]] "I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith" (2 Timothy 4:7); against "Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall" (Proverbs 16:18).

Servant ↔ Sovereign.base:
[[Thesis]] The sixth edge axis asks who a person's strength answers to — himself, or the work in front of him — and both answers are governed rather than free.

[[Argument]] Activation and Self-Regard are committed here in the pairing Lion ↔ Lamb leaves out. The Sovereign end joins Composure to Dignity: restraint exercised by someone who holds his own worth high, which is Self-Mastery — the rule of a man over himself, the oldest form of rule the tradition recognizes. The Servant end joins Vigor to Humility: force spent by someone who holds his own worth low, which is Diligence — the work done because it is there to be done. The axis is the cube's answer to a confusion that runs through every account of authority: mastery of oneself and service of others are not opposite virtues but opposite ends of one line, and the man in the middle has neither. Their falls are unusually easy to mistake for the virtues. Self-Mastery becomes Disdain when the government of oneself turns into a measurement of everyone else, so that standing is now held by contempt. Diligence becomes Servility when the work is done for the pleasure of whoever ordered it rather than because it was worth doing — the fall that gave a language two proper names for it, one English and one Norwegian.

[[Correspondences]] Cold end (−1,0,+1): Self-Mastery falling to Disdain — Odysseus and Bruce Lee against Coriolanus and Diogenes. Warm end (+1,0,−1): Diligence falling to Servility — Martha of Bethany and Mother Teresa against Uriah Heep and Vidkun Quisling. On the Rose the two seats face each other at 19h in red and 07h in blue; on the Almanac wheel the axis takes September at 18h — the autumn equinox, and the Ruler's own hour.

[[Quote]] "He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city" (Proverbs 16:32); "whosoever will be chief among you, let him be your servant" (Matthew 20:27).

Self-Mastery.base:
[[Thesis]] Self-Mastery is the Sovereign cell of the Servant ↔ Sovereign axis: a person's own strength governed by himself, in advance of the moment it would be needed.

[[Argument]] The seat joins Composure to Dignity — restraint exercised by someone who holds his worth high — and its archetypal act is the tradition's own image of self-government: a man binds himself to the mast and stops his crew's ears before the song begins, which is the discipline arranged in advance rather than summoned in the moment. Bruce Lee is seated on the training notebooks and the daily regime, the historical form of the same thing: a body ruled by a written rule its owner set. Uncle Iroh walks away from a throne he could have taken, which is the modern reading — the rule of oneself proved by what is declined. The fall changes the object of the measurement. Disdain is Self-Mastery turned outward: a man who has governed himself begins to grade everyone who has not, and his standing is now held by contempt rather than by conduct. Coriolanus will not show his wounds to people he despises; a philosopher tells the greatest man alive to stand out of his light and carries a lamp at noon looking for a man; a modern lord measures kingship by the observation that any man who must say he is the king is no true king — true, and said in the tone that is the fall. The discriminator is that Self-Mastery needs no audience and Disdain requires one.

[[Correspondences]] The cell (−1,0,+1), Composure plus Dignity, on the Servant ↔ Sovereign axis, facing Diligence and its fall Servility through the centre. On the Rose it takes 19h in red; on the Almanac wheel its axis holds September at 18h, the Ruler's own hour. Archetypal: Odysseus against Coriolanus. Historical: Bruce Lee against Diogenes. Modern: Uncle Iroh against Tywin Lannister. Odysseus was also considered for Machination on the strength of the horse, and the mast was judged the better fit — a figure holds one seat.

[[Quote]] "He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls" (Proverbs 25:28); "Know thyself" (the Delphic maxim).

Diligence.base:
[[Thesis]] Diligence is the Servant cell of the Servant ↔ Sovereign axis: work done because it is there to be done, by someone who does not hold his own standing high enough to consider it beneath him.

[[Argument]] The seat joins Vigor to Humility. Its archetypal reading is the gentlest measure line in the Gospels: a woman cumbered about much serving is not rebuked for the serving, which is real and necessary, but told that it has crowded out the one thing needful — the seat and its limit stated in a single scene of a household. Mother Teresa opens Kalighat in 1952, which is the historical form of the same virtue: a work begun where the work was, without any prior arrangement about who would notice. Andy Dufresne spends nineteen years on a rock hammer and one letter a week until a library exists, and the modern reading is exact because the labour is invisible for almost all of its duration. The fall is the same work performed for the pleasure of whoever ordered it. Servility is diligence with the object changed from the task to the master: a clerk is ever so humble and the phrase became a byword for the posture; a wartime minister's surname became the common noun for ruling at another's pleasure; a house-elf punishes his own hands for the disobedience of having helped. That last reading is deliberately left as a station rather than as a verdict — he ends free, which is what a fall on a line is: a position a person can leave.

[[Correspondences]] The cell (+1,0,−1), Vigor plus Humility, on the Servant ↔ Sovereign axis, facing Self-Mastery and its fall Disdain through the centre. On the Rose it takes 07h in blue; on the Almanac wheel its axis holds September at 18h. Archetypal: Martha of Bethany against Uriah Heep. Historical: Mother Teresa against Vidkun Quisling. Modern: Andy Dufresne against Dobby. Add Loyalty to this cell and it becomes the Sacrificial Protector; add Integrity and it becomes the Principled Reformer.

[[Quote]] "Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might" (Ecclesiastes 9:10); against "No man can serve two masters" (Matthew 6:24).

The Contemplative Sage.base:
[[Thesis]] Blue, purple-gray and green — Composure, Integrity and Humility — combine into the character who holds a principle without needing to enforce it.

[[Argument]] The sage is the Cube's least coercive corner: he judges by a rule, but low activation keeps him from imposing it and humility keeps him from becoming it. Job holds the archetypal seat because the entire book is a man maintaining a position under a pressure designed to break it, without once taking action against anyone. The fall is the Paralyzed Purist, where the same restraint that made him fair makes him useless — Hamlet's exact seat, and the reason Hamlet is not seated at the blue pole: his problem is not that he lacks vitality but that he cannot act without a purity he cannot obtain.

[[Correspondences]] Positive against fallen — Job against Hamlet; Leo Tolstoy against Nicholas II; Gandalf against Mace Windu. On the Character wheel the corner reads flat as Renunciation, falling to Mortification.

[[Quote]] "Though he slay me, yet will I trust in him" (Job 13:15).

The Charismatic Champion.base:
[[Thesis]] Orange, yellow and red — Vigor, Loyalty and Dignity — combine into the character a people follows because he is plainly one of them and plainly larger.

[[Argument]] This is the corner of the leader in the field. Vigor makes him act, loyalty makes the action be for a specific people, and dignity makes the people willing to be led. Churchill is the historical case because the war he is remembered for was fought first as rhetoric. The fall is the Tribal Warlord, where the same three harden: vigor into appetite for the fight itself, loyalty into enmity toward everyone outside, dignity into a cult. Agamemnon is exact — the king of a coalition who spends it on his own honour.

[[Correspondences]] Positive against fallen — Beowulf against Agamemnon; Winston Churchill against Benito Mussolini; Wonder Woman against Khal Drogo. On the Character wheel the corner reads flat as Patronage, falling to Favoritism.

[[Quote]] "The people had a mind to work" (Nehemiah 4:6).

Vow ↔ Vision.base:
[[Thesis]] The first of the three human vertex axes runs between the character who keeps what he was given and the character who founds what nobody gave him — three axes committed at each end, and every one of them reversed across the line.

[[Argument]] A vertex commits all three axes at once, so its two ends differ in everything: the Quiet Devotee is Composure, Loyalty and Humility together, the Visionary Founder is Vigor, Integrity and Dignity together. That total reversal is what makes the diagonal axes the strongest lines on the cube and the hardest to hold in one description. The Vow end is the quietest corner of the whole figure: a person who does not need to act, judges by his bonds and holds his own worth low will spend a life inside one household and count it well spent. The Vision end is the loudest: a person who acts, judges by a principle and knows his own standing will make something that did not exist, and will require other people to live inside it. Their falls are the same three directions carried past measure. The Devotee's composure becomes inertia, his loyalty an inability to refuse, his humility the conviction that his objection would not matter — the Submissive Enabler, whose distance from the virtue is not a change of direction but the loss of the standing to say no. The Founder's vigour becomes ceaseless motion, his integrity a code answerable to nobody, his dignity a claim about himself — the Messianic Tyrant, the man who crowns himself, writes the law and never stops.

[[Correspondences]] Cold end (−1,+1,−1): the Quiet Devotee falling to the Submissive Enabler — the Virgin Mary, Florence Nightingale and Faramir against Ophelia, Eva Braun and Peter Pettigrew. Warm end (+1,−1,+1): the Visionary Founder falling to the Messianic Tyrant — Aeneas, Mustafa Kemal Atatürk and Leia Organa against the Pharaoh of the Exodus, Napoleon Bonaparte and Paul Atreides. On the Rose the corners face each other at 10h in green and 22h in rose; on the Almanac wheel the axis takes December at 24h — the winter solstice, the vow kept and the vision begun.

[[Quote]] "When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it" (Ecclesiastes 5:4); "Where there is no vision, the people perish" (Proverbs 29:18).

The Quiet Devotee.base:
[[Thesis]] Blue, yellow and green — Composure, Loyalty and Humility — combine into the character that serves a bond without needing to be seen doing it.

[[Argument]] The three directions reinforce each other unusually cleanly here: a person who does not need to act, judges by his bonds and holds his worth low will spend a life inside one household and count it well spent. The vertex is the quietest corner of the Cube, and its fall is the same three carried past measure — the Submissive Enabler, whose composure has become inertia, whose loyalty has become inability to refuse, and whose humility has become the conviction that his objection would not matter. The distance between the two is not a change of direction but a loss of the one thing the devotee must retain: the standing to say no.

[[Correspondences]] Positive against fallen — Virgin Mary against Ophelia; Florence Nightingale against Eva Braun; Faramir against Peter Pettigrew. On the Character wheel the same corner, with the Activation axis dropped, is the seat of Devotion and its fall Martyrdom.

[[Quote]] "Behold the handmaid of the Lord" (Luke 1:38).

The Visionary Founder.base:
[[Thesis]] Orange, purple-gray and red — Vigor, Integrity and Dignity — combine into the character who builds a new order and is willing to be identified with it.

[[Argument]] All three directions are at their most forward here, which makes this the Cube's most productive corner and its most dangerous. Aeneas leaves a burning city to found another; Atatürk rewrites an alphabet. The fall, the Messianic Tyrant, is what the same corner becomes when the founder concludes that the order and his own person are the same fact: vigor never stops, integrity becomes a code he authors, dignity becomes worship. Napoleon's true seat is here rather than at the red pole — the man who crowns himself, writes the code, and never stops.

[[Correspondences]] Positive against fallen — Aeneas against the Pharaoh of the Exodus; Mustafa Kemal Atatürk against Napoleon Bonaparte; Leia Organa against Paul Atreides (Daenerys Targaryen is the recorded alternate). On the Character wheel the corner reads flat as Conviction and Dignity together, falling to Dogmatism and Self-Worship.

[[Quote]] "Where there is no vision, the people perish" (Proverbs 29:18).

Preservation ↔ Revolution.base:
[[Thesis]] The second human vertex axis runs between the character who keeps a thing standing and the character who overturns it on principle — and the two corners it joins are the same two the dial already draws as its hexagram.

[[Argument]] The Preservation corner is Composure, Loyalty and Dignity: a person who does not move first, judges by his bonds and knows his own standing will hold an inheritance together, and will be the reason it survives a bad generation. The Revolution corner is Vigor, Integrity and Humility: a person who acts, judges by a rule and does not press his own claim will break an arrangement that a rule condemns, and will not require the credit. Neither is the other's fall, which is the whole reason this axis exists in a canon that also draws two crosses: continuity and overturning are the same axis walked in two directions, not virtue against vice. The falls are precise. The Guardian's own strengths, kept past their measure, produce the Complacent Nepotist — the inheritance now defended for the sake of those who hold it rather than for its own sake, which is preservation that has forgotten what it preserves. The Reformer's, carried past his, produce the Puritanical Zealot — the correction now enjoyed, the rule enforced past every human case it was written to serve. Geometry gives this axis a second name: its two ends are the Court and Genesis corners, so the Offices view of the cube looks straight down this line.

[[Correspondences]] Cold end (−1,+1,+1): the Steady Guardian falling to the Complacent Nepotist — Hector, Queen Elizabeth II and Aragorn against King Lear, Louis XV and Denethor II. Warm end (+1,−1,−1): the Principled Reformer falling to the Puritanical Zealot — Antigone, Martin Luther King Jr. and Luke Skywalker against Judge Claude Frollo, Girolamo Savonarola and Stannis Baratheon. On the Rose the corners face each other at 14h in orange and 02h in cyan; on the Almanac wheel the axis takes April at 8h, Easter's month and the great overturning.

[[Quote]] "Remove not the ancient landmark, which thy fathers have set" (Proverbs 22:28); against "Behold, I make all things new" (Revelation 21:5).

The Steady Guardian.base:
[[Thesis]] Blue, yellow and red — Composure, Loyalty and Dignity — combine into the character that holds a position on behalf of people who did not choose him.

[[Argument]] This is the corner of inherited duty: low activation makes him a keeper rather than a founder, loyalty binds him to a specific house, and dignity makes the keeping an office instead of a habit. Hector defends a city he knows is doomed and does not leave; Elizabeth II reigned for seventy years in an office defined entirely by not acting. The fall is the Complacent Nepotist, in whom the same three decay in place — composure into idleness, loyalty into favour for his own, and dignity into the belief that the office is a possession. Lear is exact because he divides a kingdom by declarations of love and is astonished when the office does not follow him out the door.

[[Correspondences]] Positive against fallen — Hector against King Lear; Queen Elizabeth II against Louis XV; Aragorn against Denethor II. On the Character wheel the corner reads flat as Patronage, falling to Favoritism.

[[Quote]] "He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much" (Luke 16:10).

The Principled Reformer.base:
[[Thesis]] Orange, purple-gray and green — Vigor, Integrity and Humility — combine into the character who acts on a principle and does not exempt himself from it.

[[Argument]] It is the Cube's engine of change. The rule comes first, the action follows, and humility is what keeps the reformer from becoming the reform's own beneficiary — Antigone buries her brother and expects the sentence; King writes from the jail he was warned about. The fall is the Puritanical Zealot, where the exemption quietly appears: vigor becomes campaign, integrity becomes a purity test, and the humility that once applied the rule to himself now applies it only outward. Frollo is exact because he is certain the fire is impersonal.

[[Correspondences]] Positive against fallen — Antigone against Judge Claude Frollo; Martin Luther King Jr. against Girolamo Savonarola; Luke Skywalker against Stannis Baratheon. On the Character wheel the corner reads flat as Conviction, falling to Dogmatism.

[[Quote]] "Let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream" (Amos 5:24).

Crown ↔ Shield.base:
[[Thesis]] The third human vertex axis runs between the character who governs from a distance and the character who puts his body between a danger and somebody else.

[[Argument]] The Crown corner is Composure, Integrity and Dignity: restraint, principle and standing together produce the man who decides for people he will never meet, and whose whole discipline is to keep his judgment further from his own interests than his office requires. The Shield corner is Vigor, Loyalty and Humility: force, bond and low self-regard produce the man who spends himself on the people directly in front of him. The axis therefore holds the oldest political argument in the canon — rule against protection — as a line rather than as a dispute, and the two ends need each other exactly as the two triangles of the hexagram do. Their falls are the two failures of every office. Distance carried past measure produces the Cold Elitist, whose judgment is now protected from the people it governs. Protection carried past measure produces the Fanatical Martyr, whose paying has outgrown whatever was being paid for. The symmetry law seats this axis on the Rose's own horizontal — the Statesman on the Ruler's hour and the Protector on the Servant's — which the canon accepted as its second symbolic choice rather than as an accident: the crown to the one who governs, the shield to the one who serves.

[[Correspondences]] Cold end (−1,−1,+1): the Wise Statesman falling to the Cold Elitist — Joseph son of Jacob, George Washington and Albus Dumbledore against the Grand Inquisitor, Klemens von Metternich and Saruman. Warm end (+1,+1,−1): the Sacrificial Protector falling to the Fanatical Martyr — Moses, Harriet Tubman and Harry Potter against Samson, Yukio Mishima and Kylo Ren. On the Rose the corners face each other at 18h in red and 06h in blue, the Sunday axis' own two seats; on the Almanac wheel the axis takes August at 16h — Augustus's own month.

[[Quote]] "Fear not, Abram: I am thy shield, and thy exceeding great reward" (Genesis 15:1); "Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown" (Shakespeare, Henry IV, Part 2).

The Wise Statesman.base:
[[Thesis]] Blue, purple-gray and red — Composure, Integrity and Dignity — combine into the character who governs by rule and knows the rule outranks him.

[[Argument]] It is the Cube's most institutional corner. Composure keeps him from reacting, integrity gives him a law to answer to, and dignity gives him standing to enforce it — the combination that writes constitutions rather than manifestos. Washington's decisive act was a resignation. The fall is the Cold Elitist, where the same three sour: composure into distance, integrity into a code the governed have no share in, dignity into caste. The Grand Inquisitor is exact because he argues, sincerely and at length, that the rule is for everyone's good and that nobody else may be trusted with it.

[[Correspondences]] Positive against fallen — Joseph son of Jacob against The Grand Inquisitor; George Washington against Klemens von Metternich; Albus Dumbledore against Saruman. On the Character wheel the corner reads flat as Conviction, falling to Dogmatism.

[[Quote]] "Righteousness exalteth a nation: but sin is a reproach to any people" (Proverbs 14:34).

The Sacrificial Protector.base:
[[Thesis]] Orange, yellow and green — Vigor, Loyalty and Humility — combine into the character who spends himself for his own and asks nothing back.

[[Argument]] High activation turns devotion into action: this corner does not keep the household, it carries it out of danger. Moses argues with God on behalf of a people that has just disowned him, which is the seat in one sentence. The fall is the Fanatical Martyr, in whom the same three run past measure — vigor into compulsion, loyalty into an attachment that admits no other claim, humility into the conviction that his own destruction is the proof required. Samson's last act is exact: he pulls the house down and is inside it.

[[Correspondences]] Positive against fallen — Moses against Samson; Harriet Tubman against Yukio Mishima; Harry Potter against Kylo Ren (Anakin Skywalker is the recorded alternate). On the Character wheel the corner reads flat as Devotion, falling to Martyrdom.

[[Quote]] "Yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book" (Exodus 32:32).

The Hexagram Projection.base:
[[Thesis]] Looked at along a body diagonal, the cube projects as the hexagonal framework the six-pointed star is constructed from — so the emblem at the centre of this dial is the Character Cube seen end-on.

[[Argument]] The projection is exact rather than suggestive. The silhouette of a cube viewed along a main diagonal is a regular hexagon; the six spokes that reach its corners are the two polar corners' own edges; and the star's two triangles are the six equatorial face-diagonals, one contributed by each face, every one of them perpendicular to the view. Two viewing directions are named because each teaches something different. Along the Court and Genesis corners — which are the two ends of the Preservation ↔ Revolution axis — the upward triangle is the Court trio's diagonals and the downward one is the Genesis trio's, which is the hexagram this dial has always drawn. Along the Sacred Axis the arrangement turns pure: all three sacred seats fall onto the single centre point, so the axle is that axis seen end-on and the hands rotate around it, the cold Christic triangle faces the warm Diabolic one, and the hexagon's six ring corners are the six human vertices — God at the axle and mankind on the ring. There are two such directions, one from each absolute corner, and the cube does not change between them; only the viewpoint does. From either corner exactly seven cells are hidden — the antipode with its three edges and its three faces, nineteen visible against seven hidden out of twenty-six — which is the blindness law: the Advocate and the Prosecutor cannot see into each other's court, and only the centre sees all twenty-six.

[[Correspondences]] The hexagon is the dial's own six arms and the star its own emblem; the three primary axes are the diagonals 12h–24h, 16h–04h and 20h–08h. The Sacred Axis projects to the axle, which is why the sacred trio displays at the centre and never on a human hour. The blindness law is the same doctrine the Double Trinity states when it gives the whole vertical to God alone: the Judge reads both files.

[[Quote]] "The Cube is the world of character; the Hexagram is what that world reveals when viewed along the Sacred Axis"; "and the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not" (John 1:5).

The Banknote Axes.base:
[[Thesis]] The six letters the owner's hexagram picks out of the Great Seal's mottos are not an ornament on the Cube: their three oppositions ARE the Cube's three axes.

[[Argument]] The Canon had already read the letter pairs as doctrine — A against M as Humility against Pride, N against S as the Nazarene against Satan, G against Omega as beginning against end — and each of those readings turns out to name one axis exactly. A against M is the Self-Regard line. N against S is Activation: stillness against storm, the stilled sea against the mustered host. G against Omega is Moral Scope: covenant against law, the God who binds himself to a people against the letter that will not pass away. Three independent constructions — a banknote's hexagram, a dial's six arms and a three-axis account of character — land on the same six oppositions, which is the strongest internal evidence this system has that its geometry was not chosen arbitrarily.

[[Correspondences]] G, yellow, Loyalty: the God of the covenant, shadowed by Tribalism. Omega, purple-gray, Integrity: the law that holds to the last, shadowed by Legalism. A, green, Humility: the beginning and the ministering spirit, shadowed by Self-Annihilation. M, red, Dignity: mastery rightly worn, shadowed by Self-Worship. N, blue, Composure: the accepted cup, shadowed by Lethargy. S, orange, Vigor: Sigma the sum, the God of armies, shadowed by Frenzy. The blue shadow is this application's own counter-motto — the fall of the watchful color is the failure to keep watch, and answering that failure is what the instrument is for.

[[Quote]] "What I say unto you I say unto all, Watch" (Mark 13:37).

The Double Trinity.base:
[[Thesis]] Three persons hold six offices — three judicial and three creative — and the two triangles they form are the hexagram itself.

[[Argument]] The construction is the oldest in this canon and the simplest: God, Jesus and the Devil each sit twice, once on the upward triangle and once on its counter-triangle, so that the six arms of the dial are three persons doubled rather than six characters listed. The upward triangle is the Court: Judge, Advocate, Prosecutor. The downward is Genesis: Creator, Preserver, Destroyer. Their order is not decorative — JUDGMENT PRECEDES TRANSFORMATION. The Court decides what deserves to remain; creation then makes, keeps and unmakes accordingly, which is why the creation triangle is drawn beneath the judicial one and why a Destroyer who acts before the verdict is committing Frenzy rather than performing an office. God alone holds a full diameter, the 12h-24h vertical; the other two hold diagonals, and those diagonals cross the persons: Advocate against Destroyer, Prosecutor against Preserver — defense against unmaking, accusation against keeping.

[[Correspondences]] 12h yellow, God the Judge; 24h purple-gray, God the Creator; 04h blue, Jesus the Advocate; 08h green, Jesus the Preserver; 20h red, the Devil the Prosecutor; 16h orange, the Devil the Destroyer. The vertical is the Banknote's G against Omega, Revelation 1:8 drawn as geometry. THE MANY-NAMES DOCTRINE governs the reading: God and The One are the same person under names that are deliberately kept apart — the Court wheel says The One, this canon and the Genesis and Council wheels say God — because a plurality of names presents him as more than a single personality. The system never reconciles the names; it layers them.

[[Quote]] "I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, saith the Lord, which is, and which was, and which is to come" (Revelation 1:8).

The Court.base:
[[Thesis]] The upward triangle — 12h, 04h and 20h — is a courtroom, and it is the first of the two triangles because nothing may be transformed before it has been judged.

[[Argument]] A court requires exactly three offices and no more: one who accuses, one who defends, one who decides. The dial gives each an hour that argues for it. The Judge sits at noon, the present — the only position from which a case can actually be heard, since the past no longer happens and the future has not yet. The Advocate sits at 04h, the arm of the past, because a defense always pleads deeds already done. The Prosecutor sits at 20h, the arm of the future, because an accusation is always a claim about what the accused would go on to be. The three natures follow from the offices rather than being attached to them: the Judge must hold both love of self and love of others or he can be steered; the Advocate is love turned outward until it costs him; the Prosecutor is love turned back on itself.

[[Correspondences]] Yellow, blue and red — the Trinity paint wheel, whose centre is the Eye of Providence: objectivity as the only glass that does not tint the light through it. The same three arms are the Banknote's G, N and M — God, the Nazarene, the Master. On the Cube the triangle is one corner of the cube, yellow above with blue and red beside it.

[[Quote]] "Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?" (Genesis 18:25).

Genesis.base:
[[Thesis]] The downward triangle — 24h, 08h and 16h — is the creation wheel: the same three persons acting on substance instead of on a case.

[[Argument]] What the Court has decided, Genesis executes, and it takes exactly three motions to do so: make, keep, unmake. God creates at midnight, because the first act recorded of creation is performed over an unlit deep — making is prior to light, not a consequence of it. Jesus preserves on the green arm, the humble office that adds nothing of its own and is the reason the wheel is a balance rather than a sequence. The Devil destroys on the orange arm, and the office is legitimate: a world that could only accumulate would collapse under itself. The triangle is drawn inverted for the same reason it is drawn second — it stands under the Court's verdict, not beside it.

[[Correspondences]] Purple-gray, green and orange — the second corner of the Cube, opposite the Court's. Its centre is The Beginning: where the Court's centre watches what already exists, the creation centre is the first act itself. The Path of Light terminates on this triangle's midnight arm, which is why a bright road ends remade rather than acquitted, "a new creature" (2 Corinthians 5:17). Its wheel sits in the third slot of the Trinity pointer, beside the Court and the Family.

[[Quote]] "In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth" (Genesis 1:1).

The Council.base:
[[Thesis]] The Council is the union: all six offices seated at once, the two triangles interlocked into the star.

[[Argument]] Separately the triangles argue a sequence; together they argue a session. The claim of the union wheel is that judgment and creation are not two departments but one body — the person who decides what deserves to remain is the person who must then make what replaces what did not, and the office that accuses is the office that unmakes. Only in the union does the structure become visible: three persons, six chairs, one diameter and two diagonals. The diameter belongs to God because a judge who also creates cannot disown his sentence; the diagonals cross the persons, so that no one argues with himself and everyone answers someone.

[[Correspondences]] The six arms of the Prism read as offices: God the Judge at noon and God the Creator at midnight; the Devil the Destroyer at 16h and the Prosecutor at 20h; Jesus the Advocate at 04h and the Preserver at 08h. The centre is the Lord's Day — six offices as the six days of work, the seventh seat as the rest that completes them. Its anchor is the divine council in session, and its wheel sits in the third slot of the Prism pointer, beside Paint and Light.

[[Quote]] "God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods" (Psalm 82:1).

The Twenty-Four Fields.base:
[[Thesis]] The six offices expand to twenty-four: twelve outer offices and twelve inner processes, four of each per person — the Double Trinity's full machinery, too rich for a dial and exactly the size of an encyclopedia page.

[[Argument]] Each of the six seats is a summary of four. The office names what a person DOES; the process names what happens to the object he does it to — so every pair reads as an act and its effect. The division by four is not arbitrary but forced: three persons over twelve offices leaves four each, and the six core seats are simply the two most characteristic of each person's four. Read as a wheel the twelve pairs run continuously from judgment through ruin and back through renewal, which is the same circuit the Two Crosses walk on foot: the fields are the machinery, the crosses are the journey.

[[Correspondences]] GOD holds Judge/Justice, Avenger/Retribution, Creator/Reinvention and Lawgiver/Reform. THE DEVIL holds Destroyer/Punishment, Tempter/Ruin, Prosecutor/Guilt and Catalyst/Critique. JESUS holds Redeemer/Renewal, Advocate/Salvation, Shepherd/Mercy and Preserver/Stewardship. The four-and-four pattern preserves the hexagram's own logic: God's four are the two ends of the vertical plus their instruments, and the diagonals keep crossing the persons — the Advocate's Salvation stands against the Destroyer's Punishment, the Prosecutor's Guilt against the Preserver's Stewardship.

[[Quote]] "To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven" (Ecclesiastes 3:1).

The Two Crosses.base:
[[Thesis]] Two four-station journeys run on the hexagram's arms — an upward cross and a downward cross that share the vertical — and each ends in the other's hour.

[[Argument]] A seat is what an arm IS; a station is where a traveller STANDS at that hour of a journey, and the arm hosts the station as an inn hosts a walker. That distinction is what lets both crosses use the same six arms without displacing the Prism's own occupants. The Path of Light runs 08h, 12h, 16h, 24h — Hope, Faith, Love, Salvation. The Path of Darkness runs 20h, 24h, 04h, 12h — Fear, Anger, Hate, Suffering. THE CHIASM is the pair's whole argument: the bright road ends at midnight and the dark road ends at noon, so neither journey terminates in its own kind of hour. The Double Trinity names why. Noon is God as JUDGE, so the dark path ends exposed before the Judge; midnight is God as CREATOR, so the light path ends remade in the Creator's hands. Every road, bright or dark, terminates on God's own axis.

[[Correspondences]] Latin rows: TIMOR, IRA, ODIUM, DOLOR for the descent; SPES, FIDES, CARITAS, SALUS for the ascent. Greek rows: PHOBOS, ORGE, MISOS, PATHOS; ELPIS, PISTIS, AGAPE, SOTERIA. The two readings sealed for the pair: suffering is what grew in secret while the blanket was pulled over fear, wrath and hate, and then stepped into daylight; salvation is what grew quietly while the day was worked in faith, hope and love, and arrived unannounced at midnight.

[[Quote]] "And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not" (John 1:5).

The Path of Light.base:
[[Thesis]] The upward cross is not a reward for virtue but the ordinary shape of a day worked in trust: hope at dawn, faith at noon, love at evening, salvation at midnight.

[[Argument]] Its stations are the three theological virtues in their natural order of appearance, closed by the thing they were for. Hope comes first because it is the smallest — the seed and the sprout — and nothing else can start before something has survived the night. Faith stands at noon because faith is upright posture under full light, not a refuge from it. Love takes the evening arm because love in this canon is a DEED rather than a sentiment: the vow made, the table set, the guardian's own hour. Salvation arrives at midnight and is deliberately not placed at the summit — the road does not climb into daylight, it walks through to the Creator's hour and is remade there.

[[Correspondences]] 08h green, Hope — the Preserver's arm and the Banknote's Alpha. 12h yellow, Faith — the Judge's arm and the present. 16h orange, Love — the Destroyer's arm read as vigor spent for another. 24h, Salvation — the Creator's arm, which the Ages wheel already dresses in the white of a death that goes into the light. Its centre is TRUST; its cipher, read from the summit back down, is SAFE.

[[Quote]] "Now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity" (1 Corinthians 13:13).

Hope.base:
[[Thesis]] Hope is the first station of the Path of Light because it is the smallest thing capable of surviving a night.

[[Argument]] Every other station presupposes something already alive. Hope is what is left when a case for optimism cannot be made — the seed in the ground, which is the same figure the Banknote's Alpha carries on this arm, and the sprout, which is the smallest visible claim that the ground has not won. It is seated at the morning arm because hope rises humbly rather than triumphantly, and at the beginning of the journey because it is the only virtue that costs nothing to start and everything to abandon.

[[Correspondences]] 08h green — Jesus' Preserver seat in the Double Trinity, the Humility pole of the Cube's Self-Regard axis, the Prism's arm of Renewal, and the Banknote's A. Its Latin name is SPES, its Greek ELPIS; it is the S of the STAR mnemonic's Spark and the E of the SAFE cipher's Elpis. Its opposite number on the dark cross is Hate at 04h — the grudge that refuses to let the past pass, against the seed that refuses to let the future close.

[[Quote]] "Hope that is seen is not hope: for what a man seeth, why doth he yet hope for?" (Romans 8:24).

Faith.base:
[[Thesis]] Faith is the noon station because faith is standing upright under full light, not sheltering from it.

[[Argument]] The station is often mistaken for credulity, which would belong in the dark; the definition this canon uses is the one given in Hebrews — substance and evidence, the words of a court rather than of a mood. That is why it is seated on the Judge's own arm and at the hour of the present: faith is a position held where everything is visible and nothing is deniable. It is also the second station rather than the first because faith without a prior hope has nothing to be faithful to.

[[Correspondences]] 12h yellow — God's Judge seat, the Loyalty pole of the Cube's Moral Scope axis, the Banknote's G, the Prism's arm of Joy. Latin FIDES, Greek PISTIS; the T of STAR (Trust) stands in its place in the mnemonic, and the F of SAFE is its own. Directly opposite it on the dark cross is Suffering, which occupies the same hour: the two crosses share noon, and the difference between them there is the difference between standing in the light and being exposed by it.

[[Quote]] "Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen" (Hebrews 11:1).

Love.base:
[[Thesis]] Love takes the evening arm of vigor because love in this canon is a deed and not a sentiment.

[[Argument]] The station is placed on the Destroyer's own arm deliberately: the same force that unmakes is the force that, turned toward another, builds — and the canon's test for love is expenditure, not feeling. The evening hour carries the vow made and the table set, the two acts by which a household is actually constituted; the arm is also the guardian's, the archangel's own. Love is the third station because it is the one that costs, and a road that asked for it first would be asking for a payment before any wage had been earned.

[[Correspondences]] 16h orange — the Devil's Destroyer seat, the Vigor pole of the Cube's Activation axis, the Banknote's S, the Prism's arm of Courage. Latin CARITAS, Greek AGAPE; the A of both mnemonics — Affection in STAR, Agape in SAFE. Its counterpart on the dark cross is Anger at 24h, which is what the same force becomes when it is spent against rather than for.

[[Quote]] "Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends" (John 15:13).

Salvation.base:
[[Thesis]] Salvation is placed at midnight, and its placement is the light cross' whole argument: the road does not end in daylight.

[[Argument]] A journey of hope, faith and love that terminated at noon would say that goodness is rewarded with more visibility, which is neither true nor interesting. Ending it at the darkest hour says something harder and better attested — that what was worked in the day arrives unannounced in the night, and that the hour of the Creator is where a person is remade rather than merely acquitted. The scriptural record keeps the hour: the prison doors open at midnight, and the tomb is found empty while it is yet dark.

[[Correspondences]] 24h — God's Creator seat, the Integrity pole of the Cube's Moral Scope axis, the Banknote's Omega, and the arm the Ages wheel dresses in pure white because in the light register death goes INTO the light. Latin SALUS, Greek SOTERIA; the R of STAR (Redemption) and the S of SAFE. It shares its arm with Anger, the dark cross' second station — the same midnight holding a wrath that would not sleep and a deliverance that arrived while everyone did.

[[Quote]] "And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God... and immediately all the doors were opened" (Acts 16:25-26).

The Path of Darkness.base:
[[Thesis]] The downward cross is a sequence with a mechanism: fear cools into anger, anger freezes into hate, and what was hidden is exposed at noon as suffering.

[[Argument]] Its stations are not four separate evils but one process observed at four hours. Fear is the dark reading of what is coming. Anger is fear that has found an object and been kept overnight. Hate is anger that has cooled and been decided — no longer hot, and therefore no longer self-limiting. Suffering is not a fifth emotion but the bill: what fermented in the dark standing naked in full light. The path therefore descends through the night in the literal sense, dusk to midnight to before-dawn, and then walks into the day it has been avoiding.

[[Correspondences]] 20h red, Fear — the future's arm. 24h purple-gray, Anger — the livid hour. 04h blue, Hate — the past's arm. 12h, Suffering — the Judge's noon. Its centre is DISTRUST; its cipher, assembled rather than walked, is DOMY — the application's own name. Latin: TIMOR, IRA, ODIUM, DOLOR. Greek: PHOBOS, ORGE, MISOS, PATHOS.

[[Quote]] "For the thing which I greatly feared is come upon me" (Job 3:25).

Fear.base:
[[Thesis]] Fear is the dark cross' first station because every descent begins as a reading of the future rather than of the present.

[[Argument]] The station is seated at dusk on the arm the Triads already read as the future, and the placement is the argument: fear is not a response to what is happening but a forecast of what will. That is also why it is first — nothing in the chain below it can start until something has been anticipated. Job's line is quoted for its grammar as much as its content: the feared thing arrives, and the fearing did not prevent it. The red arm is the predator hour and the blood-red west, and the same arm carries Dignity's fall at the pole — the self that fears for itself first.

[[Correspondences]] 20h red — the Devil's Prosecutor seat, the Dignity pole of the Cube's Self-Regard axis, the Banknote's M, the Prism's arm of Passion. Latin TIMOR (and METUS, the second Latin fear-word, which supplies the M of the DOMY cipher); Greek PHOBOS; the F of the FALL mnemonic. Across the dial its cure is the light cross' Hope on the green arm — the same 20h-08h diagonal the Cube reads as Self-Regard.

[[Quote]] "For the thing which I greatly feared is come upon me, and that which I was afraid of is come unto me" (Job 3:25).

Anger.base:
[[Thesis]] Anger is the midnight station because anger is fear that has been kept overnight.

[[Argument]] The station names a threshold rather than an emotion: the instruction not to let the sun go down upon wrath describes a deadline, and this arm is the hour at which the deadline has already passed. What was still a reaction at dusk has become a possession by midnight. The colour argues the same point from language: LIVIDUS is Latin for bruise-purple and for rage at once, and more than one living tongue still says a man went purple with anger. The station shares its arm with the light cross' Salvation, which is the sharpest of the crossings — one traveller is remade at midnight and the other is nursing what he refused to put down.

[[Correspondences]] 24h purple-gray — God's Creator seat, the Integrity pole of the Cube's Moral Scope axis, the Banknote's Omega. Latin IRA; Greek ORGE, whose kin HYBRIS supplies the Y of the DOMY cipher; the A of the FALL mnemonic. Its light-cross counterpart is Love at 16h — the same force spent for another rather than kept against one.

[[Quote]] "Let not the sun go down upon your wrath" (Ephesians 4:26).

Hate.base:
[[Thesis]] Hate is the pre-dawn station because hate is anger that has cooled, and cooling is what makes it permanent.

[[Argument]] Heat limits wrath: it exhausts itself. Cold does not, which is why the station sits at the hour before dawn rather than at any hot hour, and why the language for it is cold-blooded, frozen, decided. The arm is the Triads' own past, and that is the second half of the argument — a grudge is the past refusing to pass. It is also Judas' own hour, the kiss by night before cockcrow, which the Cube reads twice over: blue is his night, and the fall of his colour is the self annihilated by what it decided in the dark.

[[Correspondences]] 04h blue — Jesus' Advocate seat, the Composure pole of the Cube's Activation axis, the Banknote's N, the Prism's arm of Calm. Latin ODIUM (the O of the DOMY cipher); Greek MISOS; the L of the FALL mnemonic, Loathing. Its light-cross counterpart is Hope at 08h — the refusal to let the future close, against the refusal to let the past go.

[[Quote]] "He that hateth his brother is in darkness, and walketh in darkness, and knoweth not whither he goeth" (1 John 2:11).

Suffering.base:
[[Thesis]] Suffering is the dark cross' terminus at noon, and it is a consequence rather than a fifth emotion.

[[Argument]] The three stations before it are all performed in the dark, and the path's claim is that darkness is a storage condition and not a destination: what was kept there is not cancelled, it matures. Noon is where it is presented, because noon is the Judge's hour and the hour at which nothing is deniable. The Passion supplies the system's own precedent for the reading, since the one recorded darkening of noon happens over exactly this kind of accounting. The station shares its arm with the light cross' Faith, and the two readings of noon are the same fact from two sides: standing in the light, and being exposed by it.

[[Correspondences]] 12h — God's Judge seat, the Loyalty pole of the Cube's Moral Scope axis, the Banknote's G. Latin DOLOR (the D of the DOMY cipher); Greek PATHOS; the second L of the FALL mnemonic, Lament. The owner's sealed reading: suffering is what grew in secret while the blanket was pulled over fear, wrath and hate — and then stepped into daylight.

[[Quote]] "For nothing is secret, that shall not be made manifest; neither any thing hid, that shall not be known and come abroad" (Luke 8:17).

Trust and Distrust.base:
[[Thesis]] The hinge of both journeys is TRUST — trust, broadly, in what cannot be controlled — and the two crosses differ at their centres before they differ at any station.

[[Argument]] Neither path begins with a virtue or a vice; both begin with a posture toward what is outside one's hands. Love that cannot trust does not stop being love: it becomes fear FOR what it loves, and the descent has already started before anything has gone wrong. Adversity met with trust does not stop being adversity: it ripens into hope, and the ascent has started before anything has gone right. This is why the centres are the crosses' true subject and the stations only their itinerary — the same events send two travellers in opposite directions depending on what they did with what they could not govern. The earlier terms Clinging and Surrender were retired in favour of this single hinge.

[[Correspondences]] Dark centre: DISTRUST, subtitled Love without Trust. Light centre: TRUST, subtitled Adversity with Trust. The canonical formula is one sentence — "Without trust, even love decays into fear; with trust, even adversity ripens into hope." On the Cube the same hinge reads as the Moral Scope axis: trust is judgment that rests on a bond it cannot audit.

[[Quote]] "Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding" (Proverbs 3:5).

FALL and STAR.base:
[[Thesis]] The two paths carry English mnemonics that name their direction: the dark path FALLs to the bottom and the bright path rises to the STARs.

[[Argument]] A mnemonic earns its place only if it argues rather than merely abbreviates, and these two do. FALL spells Fear, Anger, Loathing, Lament — and the word itself is the descent's own verb, the motion the four stations describe. STAR spells Spark, Trust, Affection, Redemption — and the word is the ascent's own destination, the thing the four stations rise toward. The substitutions are deliberate: Loathing for Hate and Lament for Suffering carry the same content in the letters the descent requires, and Spark for Hope names hope at the size the station actually claims for it.

[[Correspondences]] FALL: Fear (20h), Anger (24h), Loathing (04h), Lament (12h). STAR: Spark (08h), Trust (12h), Affection (16h), Redemption (24h). The legend is required to explain both — a mnemonic nobody is told about is a private joke, and this canon's display law makes the explanation part of the article rather than an extra.

[[Quote]] "They that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever" (Daniel 12:3).

DOMY and SAFE.base:
[[Thesis]] The application's own name is the dark cross assembled, and the word for its purpose is the bright cross read backwards: DOMY keeps you SAFE.

[[Argument]] The ciphers are built by assembly rather than by walking order, exactly as MASON is assembled from the letters ringing the Banknote's hexagram. DOMY takes DOLOR (Suffering), ODIUM (Hate), METUS (Fear — Latin's second fear-word beside Timor) and HYBRIS (the wrath station's Greek name, capital upsilon). The Y is doubly sealed: it is also the littera Pythagorica, Pythagoras' letter, the fork in the road at which the two paths part — so the last letter of the watchman's name is the diagram of the choice both crosses describe. SAFE is read from the summit back down the bright road: SALUS, AGAPE, FIDES, ELPIS — the saved traveller looks back and the word under his feet spells his condition. The watchman bears the night's four names because naming the danger IS the watch.

[[Correspondences]] DOMY: Dolor 12h, Odium 04h, Metus 20h, Hybris 24h — the four dark stations, Latin and Greek mixed. SAFE: Salus 24h, Agape 16h, Fides 12h, Elpis 08h — the four bright stations, mixed the same way, mirroring DOMY on purpose. The pair formula: DOMY keeps you SAFE — the dark cross in the name of the watch, the bright cross in the word of its purpose.

[[Quote]] "What I say unto you I say unto all, Watch" (Mark 13:37).

One Soul — The Vow — The Bond.base:
[[Thesis]] The bond between a man and a woman needs no symbolism of its own: it is this dial's existing seats spoken in the dual, and the theme is the whole wheel conjugated.

[[Argument]] The engine is a single law — honesty is a trait of the individual, and trust is that same trait's counterpart in a relationship. Generalised, every pillar of a bond is a seat's VIRTUE conjugated between two persons, and every pillar's shadow is that same seat's VICE conjugated the same way. Nothing new had to be invented and nothing had to be dropped for want of a seat: the count is six because the arms are six. This is also why the theme takes the LIGHT register of the six-armed pointer rather than a wheel of its own. The paint register seats heaven's six persons — the order of the world; light seats the six pillars of a house, which is the same geometry read at the scale where two people actually live. The three names the theme carries are not competing candidates but three registers of one claim, kept together under the same many-names doctrine that keeps God and The One from being reconciled: One Soul states what the bond IS — asked what a friend is, Aristotle answered that he is one soul dwelling in two bodies; The Vow states what founds it, since a bond that was never declared is only a habit; The Bond states what it becomes once the vow has survived some years. Where one name has to stand alone it is One Soul.

[[Correspondences]] Six pillars on the six arms: Gratitude at 12h in green, Support at 16h in yellow, Passion at 20h in red, Tolerance at 24h in magenta, Trust at 04h in blue, Respect at 08h in cyan — each the light re-hue of its arm's own paint colour, each the conjugation of that arm's planetary virtue: Jupiter's Generosity, Mars' Courage, Venus' Love, Mercury's Wisdom, the Moon's Serenity, Saturn's Patience. The three diagonals are the axes of love, and each one cures across itself: Trust disarms the Fight while Support cures Suspicion (16h–04h); Gratitude cures Score-keeping while Tolerance cures Taking-for-granted (12h–24h); Passion burns away Contempt while Respect calms Jealousy (20h–08h) — the same cross-cure law the whole instrument obeys, here between two people instead of inside one. The centre is the Union, the Sun's own seat; the Child stands outside the six as the Ninth.

[[Quote]] "Charity suffereth long, and is kind... beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things" (1 Corinthians 13:4-7).

Gratitude.base:
[[Thesis]] Gratitude is the highest pillar of the bond because it is the only one that is purely an answer: it adds nothing to what the other has done, and it is nevertheless the whole reason the giving continues.

[[Argument]] Generosity is a virtue of one person; conjugated between two it becomes gratitude, because a gift is only completed when it is received as a gift. The proof of the pillar is what happens when it is withheld: giving that meets no answer does not stop out of resentment, it stops out of exhaustion, and a house in which nothing is thanked is not a cruel house but an empty one. It holds the crown of the wheel because the canon names gratitude the highest and purest form of love — purest in the strict sense that it is the one movement in a bond with no self-interest left in it at all, since what it answers has already been received. In the light register it wears green rather than the arm's own yellow, because between two people gratitude shows as GROWTH: the answer feeds the giving that produced it, and the pair grows by that circuit rather than by either half of it. Its shadow is Taking for Granted — the same gift received as though it were owed. The vice is not ingratitude in the loud sense; it is the quiet reclassification of a gift as a baseline, after which the giver can only ever fall short of a standard he himself set.

[[Correspondences]] 12h, the yellow arm's seat, re-hued green: Jupiter's Generosity conjugated, with Jupiter's Excess as the shadow spoken in the dual — excess here being the appetite that has stopped counting what it is given. Thursday, and the arm's mood is Joy. Its cure stands across the wheel at 24h: Tolerance cures Taking-for-granted, and Gratitude in turn cures Score-keeping, Tolerance's own shadow.

[[Quote]] "In every thing give thanks" (1 Thessalonians 5:18).

Support.base:
[[Thesis]] Support is courage that has changed its address: the same virtue, no longer spent at one's own frontier but at the other's.

[[Argument]] Courage is a trait of the individual — what a person does when the danger is his. Conjugated, it becomes support: standing where the danger belongs to someone else and there is nothing to be won. This is why the pillar sits on the arm of vigour rather than on a gentler one. Support is not sympathy and it is not agreement; it is deed, and it costs exactly what courage costs, which is why so many bonds hold every other pillar and fail on this one. In the light register it wears yellow — the daylight shoulder, being somebody's working light: the pillar is what the bond does in the hours when there is labour to be done, not in the hours when there is romance to be had. Its shadow is the Fight, the same force turned inward: the arm's own wrath conjugated, so that what should stand beside now stands against. The shadow is instructive precisely because it is made of the pillar's own material — a couple that never fights is more often a couple with no courage in it at all than a couple at peace, and the cure is therefore not the removal of the force but the restoration of its direction.

[[Correspondences]] 16h, the orange arm, re-hued yellow: Mars' Courage conjugated, with Mars' Wrath as the shadow in the dual. Tuesday, and the arm's mood is Zeal. Its diagonal is 16h–04h: Trust disarms the Fight, and Support in turn cures Suspicion — the two pillars that together yield Security, which is a state of the bond and never a seat on it.

[[Quote]] "Two are better than one... for if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow" (Ecclesiastes 4:9-10).

Passion.base:
[[Thesis]] Passion is the one pillar that needs no conjugating, because love embodied is already an act between two.

[[Argument]] Every other pillar is an individual virtue spoken in the dual; love is relational at the root, which is why the conjugation law leaves this seat unchanged and why the light register leaves its colour unchanged with it. Passion is love with a body — the claim that the bond is not merely agreed to but wanted, and wanted by this person rather than by anyone who would have satisfied the same argument. A bond can survive the loss of passion the way a house survives losing its fire: it stands, and it is cold. The evening hour argues for the seat as much as the colour does — it is the hour at which a household stops working and begins wanting, and the pillar belongs to the half of the day that is not administered. Its shadow needed no conjugation either: jealousy is already a two-person vice. It is passion that has turned from wanting the other into guarding him — desire converted into ownership, which is the exact point at which the pillar stops holding the bond up and starts holding it down.

[[Correspondences]] 20h, red in BOTH registers — the only arm the light wheel does not re-hue, because love requires no translation into the dual. Venus' Love conjugated, with Venus' Jealousy as the shadow, which the seat's own vice table already carried before the theme existed. Friday, and the arm's mood is Passion. Its diagonal is 20h–08h: Passion burns away Contempt, and Respect calms Jealousy.

[[Quote]] "Set me as a seal upon thine heart... for love is strong as death" (Song of Solomon 8:6).

Tolerance.base:
[[Thesis]] Tolerance is wisdom conjugated: the working knowledge that the other person is not you and never will be.

[[Argument]] Wisdom in one person is knowing the limits of one's own judgement; between two it is knowing the limits of one's own template. Two people can never love and do all the same things, and the demand that they should is not intimacy but administration. The pillar is therefore not the endurance of faults — that reading makes the other's difference into a defect to be borne — but the retirement of a category error. This theme deliberately folds understanding and empathy into this seat instead of giving each its own: all three are the same movement, the granting to the other of an interior we have no direct access to, and splitting one movement across three seats would have inflated the wheel without adding a claim. Midnight argues for the seat because it is the hour of the long conversation, the hour at which two people find out how differently they are built; the arm is the mind's own. In the light register it wears magenta, purple's neighbour on the light side. Its shadow is Score-keeping: the ledger of who gave what, selfishness that has learned arithmetic — and a ledger is exactly what appears when the difference between two people is treated as a debt one of them is running.

[[Correspondences]] 24h, the purple arm, re-hued magenta: Mercury's Wisdom conjugated, with Mercury's Greed as the shadow in the dual — greed for one's own share, counted. Wednesday, and the arm's mood is Sorrow. Its diagonal is 24h–12h: Tolerance cures Taking-for-granted, and Gratitude cures Score-keeping.

[[Quote]] "Charity... seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil" (1 Corinthians 13:5).

Trust.base:
[[Thesis]] Trust is the pillar that names the whole engine, because it is the case from which the conjugation law was read: honesty is a trait of the individual, trust is its counterpart in the relationship.

[[Argument]] Serenity in one person is calm that does not depend on circumstances; conjugated, it is calm that depends on ANOTHER person, which is a far stronger claim and a far more exposed one. The pillar is not a belief about the other's future conduct — a belief can be held privately and cheaply — but the act of leaving oneself unguarded, which is why the body proves it better than any statement: sleeping soundly beside someone is trust in its least deniable form, because sleep cannot be performed. The seat is the deepest hour of the night for exactly that reason, and it keeps blue in both registers, because serenity spoken in the dual is still serenity and its colour does not change with its grammar. Its shadow is Suspicion — the arm's own Fear conjugated, fear that has taken a person as its object. Suspicion is the most self-fulfilling of the six shadows: it produces the surveillance that produces the concealment that it then reads as proof, and a bond under it has no procedure available for clearing itself, since every reassurance is admissible as evidence for the prosecution.

[[Correspondences]] 04h, blue in both registers: the Moon's Serenity conjugated, with the Moon's Fear as the shadow in the dual. Monday, and the arm's mood is Calm. Its diagonal is 04h–16h: Trust disarms the Fight, Support cures Suspicion. Security is what the two of them yield together, and is a state of the bond rather than a pillar of it.

[[Quote]] "The heart of her husband doth safely trust in her" (Proverbs 31:11).

Respect.base:
[[Thesis]] Respect is the only pillar that cannot be produced on demand, because it is patience conjugated, and patience is a function of time.

[[Argument]] The seat's planet is time itself, and the pillar inherits the constraint exactly: what one respects, one has watched hold under conditions that could have broken it. This is why respect cannot be granted at the start of a bond and cannot be restored by decision — it is not an attitude but an accumulated finding, and it is the pillar years build and nothing else does. In the light register it wears cyan because respect keeps a clean distance: the cool clear air one leaves around what one respects. The pillar is not proximity, it is room, and the morning arm is where a household's separate work begins. Its shadow, Contempt, is the deadliest poison the bond has: the arm's Envy conjugated and hardened into a verdict on the other's worth. It is more fatal than the fight, because a fight assumes an equal on the other side while contempt has already ruled that there is none, and it is more fatal than suspicion, because suspicion still wants the other to be innocent. Once the verdict is in, every one of the remaining five pillars is being held up against a person the holder has privately demoted.
